plan: SPEED_ARCHITECTURE_PLAN_2026-07.md stage B (L1 store + L2 assembly wired into build_sumo_demand)
what_changed: A whole-day window is now built as 'build the missing calendar days, then concatenate them'. Assembly is the only way a multi-day window is produced, so there is no second implementation that can drift. Sub-day windows, congestion-feedback builds and legacy-pool builds keep the direct path: their candidate pool depends on the whole window's own solution, so there is no day to store.

end_to_end_proof.harness: scratchpad b_proof.py — two overlapping 2-day windows, live release snapshotted and restored around both

cold_cost_per_day_measured.note: one calendar day, 3 variants, 288 variant-quarter solves, 10 workers

end_to_end_proof.every_hard_gate_held: 100% GEH<5 on every day and every direction variant in both windows; live release byte-restored afterwards

finding_that_changed_the_design.assumption: days of the same type share one candidate pool, so a merged window report could require identical protected-signature coverage
finding_that_changed_the_design.reality: each day resamples its own tour templates against its own profile (build_candidates._resample_reused_template_tours), so two weekdays share geometry but not the exact multiset — pools differ slightly by design
finding_that_changed_the_design.consequence: a day is calibrated against ITS OWN pool, not the union of the window's days as a monolithic build did. This is a further results-affecting difference beyond the four seeding streams, and is recorded as such in the plan.
finding_that_changed_the_design.resolution: coverage is a diagnostic, so the window reports the conservative envelope (fewest signatures, most missing per purpose) and keeps the per-day values beside it

pending_gates.golden_ab_6_2: one 11-day window built directly vs forced through cold L1 + assembly, byte-compared. The unit-scale equality is already a permanent test (tests/test_day_library.py::TestAssemblyEqualsMonolith); the full-scale run is owed.
